title: -/+ Healing the Modern Soul Appendix: Psychotherapy as Negative Space

sentences.en: Hey guys, it's Joel with the Tap Rate Therapy Collective Podcast, and if you're wondering why is this episode here,
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是“点击率疗法集体播客”的乔尔。如果你在想，为什么会突然有这一期节目，

sentences.en: why did God give me this episode for it serves no purpose and is only a source of infection that might have to be removed but shouldn't exist,
sentences.zh: 为什么上帝要给我这期节目，因为它没有任何用处，甚至只是个可能会切除、本不该存在的感染源，

sentences.en: it's because this is an appendix to the Making Meaning in the Modern World or Healing the Modern Soul series that I've been doing.
sentences.zh: 那是因为这是我一直在做的“在现代世界中寻找意义”或“疗愈现代心灵”系列的附录。

sentences.en: And I basically did that series because there's a bigger series about the whole history of psychology, but with psychology itself as kind of the character,
sentences.zh: 我基本上做那个系列是因为还有一个关于心理学整体历史的更大系列，但把心理学本身当作某种主角，

sentences.en: not like a boring dry textbook, but this thing adapting and changing.
sentences.zh: 不是那种枯燥乏味的教科书，而是这个不断适应和变化的事物。

sentences.en: If I ever finish that series that I have copious notes for, I think it'll be like my magnum opus that I have wanted to make for a super long time, it'll be really involved,
sentences.zh: 如果我能完成那个我有海量笔记的系列，我认为它将成为我长期以来一直想打造的巅峰之作，它会非常深入，

sentences.en: it'll be like some of the bigger audio podcast, multi-part mini-series event things that I like, but about my interests, and I don't have any time to do it,
sentences.zh: 就像我喜欢的一些更大型的音频播客、多部分迷你剧活动那样，但它是围绕我的兴趣展开的，而我根本没有时间去做，

sentences.en: and so I just decided that I was going to read through sort of the rough notes and talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定干脆通读一下那些粗略的笔记并聊聊它。

sentences.en: And this was sort of a rough draft of that, so what I was going to do in the appendix is just go through all the notes that I essentially didn't get to,
sentences.zh: 这算是那个系列的一个初稿，所以我在附录里要做的事情，就是过一遍那些我基本上没时间展开的笔记，

sentences.en: and clarify some of the points that it would have like slowed down the series to dig into in a more specific way, when a lot of that was about not being specific,
sentences.zh: 并阐明一些如果放进正片会拖慢节奏、无法进行更具体探讨的观点，尽管这其中很多内容恰恰是关于“不具体”的，

sentences.en: was about being kind of poetic as a point.
sentences.zh: 其核心意义在于保持某种诗意。

sentences.en: And so, I didn't want to get in the way of myself with that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不想在这上面给自己设限、妨碍自己。

sentences.en: If you haven't listened to the, you know, Making Meaning of the Modern World series, this episode probably makes little to no sense, and isn't something that you want to listen to.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有听过，你知道的，“在现代世界中寻找意义”系列，这一期节目可能完全听不懂，也没什么好听的。

sentences.en: If you listen to the Making Meaning or Healing the Modern Soul series, and was like, I don't like this, or this isn't, I don't get it, this isn't what we're normally doing,
sentences.zh: 如果你听了“寻找意义”或“疗愈现代心灵”系列，然后觉得：我不喜欢这个，或者这不对、我听不懂，这跟我们平时做的不一样，

sentences.en: you probably don't want to listen to the appendix.
sentences.zh: 那你大概率不会想听这个附录。

sentences.en: But, I'm just going to go through basically the notes that were left, that I didn't get to go through in their entirety.
sentences.zh: 不过，我基本上只是把剩下的那些没有完整讲完的笔记过一遍。

sentences.en: But, we got a lot into philosophy in that for the first time, and I basically, like, I don't like philosophy very much, like, I'm not a philosophy guy,
sentences.zh: 但在那一期里，我们史无前例地深入探讨了哲学，而我基本上——我其实不太喜欢哲学，我是说，我不是那种研究哲学的人，

sentences.en: I don't have anything against it, I like some of it, but I think the overall, especially, like, academic philosophy trend in my lifetime has been kind of like, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 我并不是对它有什么意见，其中有些我也挺喜欢，但我觉得总体上，尤其是像我这辈人经历的学院派哲学趋势，就有点……怎么说呢，

sentences.en: it's just not for me.
sentences.zh: 就是不太适合我。

sentences.en: And part of that is, I think, that a lot of the values that I have for how we should communicate and what the point of, like, intuition and soul and life and self and all that is,
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，我认为我所持有的很多价值观——关于我们应该如何沟通、直觉与灵魂、生命与自我等等的意义究竟是什么——

sentences.en: is explained to me better by people fighting about psychotherapy than people fighting about philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这些问题，看为了心理治疗争论不休的人去解释，比看为了哲学争论不休的人要解释得更好。

sentences.en: Because what happens in philosophy a ton of the time, from where I'm sitting, is that you have people that basically, like, make up a bunch of definitions for things, and then say,
sentences.zh: 因为在哲学领域，从我的角度来看，很多时候你会发现，有些人基本上就是为各种事物编造了一堆定义，然后说：

sentences.en: well, if these suppositions are all true, then here's all these, like, little logical games that we can play with them, so that I can go get, like, into law school.
sentences.zh: “好吧，如果这些前提全都是真的，那么我们就可以用它们来玩各种逻辑小游戏，这样我就可以去考法学院了。”

sentences.en: And I just, I don't get it, like, that isn't something that I want to do.
sentences.zh: 我真的、真的搞不懂，这根本不是我想做的事。

sentences.en: Then you have people that I do like, like Nietzsche and Wittgenstein, and, you know, there's a lot of humanistic and feeling-driven philosophy, too, Schopenhauer, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后也有我确实喜欢的人，比如尼采和维特根斯坦，而且，你知道的，也有很多充满人文关怀和情感驱动的哲学，比如叔本华，你知道的，

sentences.en: people like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的人。

sentences.en: And that's fine, but they usually sort of, like, speak for themselves and stand for themselves, and it's not, like, something that occupies a ton of academic philosophies' time,
sentences.zh: 这倒也行，但他们通常都是自己为自己发声、自己立论，这并不是那种占据学院派哲学大量时间的东西，

sentences.en: because they're either, like, Plato and Nietzsche, like, so vague that the point is kind of, like, a poetic, noetic experience.
sentences.zh: 因为他们要么——就像柏拉图和尼采那样——过于含糊，以至于其核心更像是一种诗意的、超验的体验。

sentences.en: And, you know, people can say, well, I like it, but they don't really get it, but there's not a lot of specificity to fight about.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，人们可以说“我很喜欢”，但他们其实并不真正理解，而且也没有多少具体的论点可供争辩。

sentences.en: And then what sucks up, like, all of the time is, like, analytical philosophy, where people make all these suppositions, and they're like, oh, but Diogenes made, like,
sentences.zh: 而那些占据了所有时间的却是分析哲学，人们提出各种假设，然后说：“哦，但是第欧根尼提出了针对各种形式的七步证明法，

sentences.en: the seven-step proofs for forms against forms, and that's the most complicated proof in all of classical philosophy, because he says, you know, if forms exist,
sentences.zh: 那是整个古典哲学中最复杂的证明，因为他说，你知道的，如果形式存在，

sentences.en: then they might be this, but then there are differences.
sentences.zh: 那么它们可能是这样的，但随后又存在差异。”

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: Like, I just, that stuff is not anything that I ever really want to get into on here.
sentences.zh: 真的，这些东西根本不是我以后想在节目里深入探讨的。

sentences.en: It's just not the kind of thing that I devote my brainpower to as the seven-step proof of Diogenes and all the stuff that I, a lot of, you know, philosophers really like.
sentences.zh: 我不会把脑力耗费在第欧根尼的七步证明法以及诸如此类的东西上，而这恰恰是很多哲学家非常喜欢的。

sentences.en: Like, something like the Schwepp podcast that goes through a lot of, like, classical philosophy in context and going through its perspectives,
sentences.zh: 比如像《韦普》播客那样，在语境中梳理大量古典哲学并探讨其不同视角，

sentences.en: that's the way that I want to approach classical philosophy.
sentences.zh: 那才是我想要接近古典哲学的方式。

sentences.en: And so that's, to me, you know, like a branch of psychology, not just, like, a system of arguments that I think is, like, turning philosophy into debate club is, like,
sentences.zh: 所以对我和来说，你知道的，这应该算是心理学的一个分支，而不是仅仅把它变成一套论证系统——我觉得把哲学变成辩论社，

sentences.en: kind of retrojective, and that, like, people were making these arguments, but that wasn't the point of what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 有点本末倒置。虽然人们过去确实在进行这些论证，但这并不是他们那样做的目的。

sentences.en: And then we've sort of made that the only point of it, because we can diagram them, um, in the same way that, like,
sentences.zh: 然后我们却把这变成了它唯一的目的，因为我们可以把它们画成图表，呃，

sentences.en: diagramming a sentence and looking at grammar is not the point of, like, talking, I don't think that diagramming logical arguments is the point of Plato at all.
sentences.zh: 就像画句子结构图和研究语法并不是对话的目的塞，我不认为把逻辑论证画成图表就是柏拉图的全部意义。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, what I am looking for, like, what I'm writing about on here, like, what I see is the point of, um, you know, because it heals trauma, essentially,
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道的，我在寻找的——比如我在这里写的东西，我所看到的意义，嗯，

sentences.en: and a lot's why a lot of writers and artists are very traumatized, is people that are able to use their intuition to see the future.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为这本质上治愈了创伤，这也是为什么许多作家和艺术家都受过严重创伤——就是那些能够利用直觉去预见未来的人。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, that's the thing that I talk about the most, um, when we did the series with Leon Krier, when we did, like,
sentences.zh: 呃，我是说，这是我谈论得最多的事情，嗯，当我们和莱昂·克里尔做那个系列时，当我们进行——

sentences.en: me talking about the Eames and their development of basically, like, furniture and culture until they're preempting this feeling, you know, they knew the internet was coming,
sentences.zh: 我谈论伊姆斯夫妇及其对家具和文化的发展，直到他们预先捕捉到这种感觉，你知道的，他们知道互联网即将到来，

sentences.en: even though they didn't know what it was.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们当时还不知道那到底是什么。

sentences.en: And this way that, um, I think is purely a psychological, you know, probably material phenomenon, but it's pretty incredible.
sentences.zh: 这种方式，呃，我认为这纯粹是一个心理学的，你知道的，可能也是物质的现象，但它非常不可思议。

sentences.en: It feels spiritual.
sentences.zh: 感觉很灵性。

sentences.en: Spiritual language applies to it.
sentences.zh: 灵性的语言适用于它。

sentences.en: And the spiritual metaphysical language might be right.
sentences.zh: 这种灵性的形而上学语言可能是对的。

sentences.en: Again, I'm a psychotherapist, not a prieSt.
sentences.zh: 再次重申，我是个心理治疗师，不是神父。

sentences.en: I don't really pick a side.
sentences.zh: 我真的不选边站队。

sentences.en: I just think it's neat.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这很有趣。

sentences.en: Um, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't think I can know.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我也不可能知道。

sentences.en: Um, and so what I'm doing is, like, looking at people like Philip K.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我做的事情是，审视像菲利普·K·迪克这样的人，就像，你知道的，嗯，

sentences.en: Dick, like, you know, um, when we talked to Andres Duany, um, a billion other artists that I really like, but that's sort of all of what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 当我们与安德雷斯·杜安尼交谈时，还有其他无数我非常喜欢的艺术家，他们所做的事情基本上都是这个。

sentences.en: And that was the point of the series on philosophy, was to look at people that were sort of saying something that they didn't think would be seen for a really long time,
sentences.zh: 这也是那个哲学系列的意义所在——去寻找那些表达了某种观点的人，他们当时认为这些观点很久都不会被人看到，

sentences.en: or they didn't think would be understood, or something that they couldn't say, you know, all of that messy stuff.
sentences.zh: 或者他们觉得不会被人理解，或者是他们无法言说的事情，所有那些混乱的东西。

sentences.en: Um, but that whole kind of, like, one of my, um, like, the most grating things for me is people that think, like, the debate club thing is productive in therapy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是整体上，呃，我最抓狂的事情之一，就是那些认为辩论社那一套在心理治疗中很有用的人。

sentences.en: Like, the people, the therapists who, like, debate patients, who, like, try and, like, make an argument and are like, well, if I'm not using logical points to refute their beliefs,
sentences.zh: 比如那些会和患者争辩的治疗师，他们试图，嗯，进行论证，然后说：“好吧，如果我不使用逻辑论证来驳斥他们的信念，

sentences.en: then how would they ever change?
sentences.zh: 那他们怎么可能会改变？”

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Have you ever seen one of your patients change?
sentences.zh: 你见过你的哪个患者改变过吗？

sentences.en: Like, like, when you get underneath, uh, the logic-making part of the brain, like,
sentences.zh: 就像，当你深入到大脑中负责制造逻辑的那部分以下，

sentences.en: when you get underneath that and you deal with the emotion that is fueling the need to be that intellectual or to double down on these beliefs, that's when people change.
sentences.zh: 当你穿透那一层去处理那些驱动着这种知识分子姿态或加倍固守这些信念的情感时，人们才会真正改变。

sentences.en: And, like, you can say, you know, well, debate club's so important because you have to diagram these proofs when you go to law school.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以说，你知道的：“噢，辩论社太重要了，因为你去法学院时必须画出这些证明的图表。”

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, you have to maybe take classical philosophy to get into law school or to, you need to understand the nature of empirical argument,
sentences.zh: 我是说，对，为了进法学院你可能得学点古典哲学，或者你需要理解实证论证的本质，

sentences.en: that you have to agree on terms and then go into something.
sentences.zh: 即你必须先就条款达成一致，然后才能深入探讨。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, but that isn't that hard.
sentences.zh: 就像，对，但那其实并不难。

sentences.en: It certainly isn't as hard as, like, a lot of people make it.
sentences.zh: 它绝对没有许多人吹嘘的那么难。

sentences.en: And as soon as you, you know, I know a lot of people that are lawyers, like, as soon as you graduate and you're actually doing law, none of that matters.
sentences.zh: 而且一旦你——我认识很多律师——一旦你毕业并真正开始执业，那些东西根本不重要。

sentences.en: What you're doing is going back to what I think the point is, which is to tell a story, you know.
sentences.zh: 你在做的事情其实是回归到我认为的核心，那就是讲故事，你知道的。

sentences.en: The thing that they'll tell you in law school is, like, the facts don't really matter.
sentences.zh: 他们在法学院会告诉你的是，事实其实并不重要。

sentences.en: You need to know how the law is applied and what the assumptions of it are.
sentences.zh: 你需要知道的是法律如何被适用以及它的假设是什么。

sentences.en: But when you're dealing with 12 people that you have to convince of something, what you – and there's a lot of kinds of law.
sentences.zh: 但当你面对必须说服其相信某事的12个人时，你——而且法律有很多种。

sentences.en: Like, I know that I'm talking about, you know, the movie Criminal Law.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在谈论的是，你知道的，电影里的刑法。

sentences.en: But, like, when you have to do that, the facts don't matter.
sentences.zh: 但是，当你必须这样做时，事实根本不重要。

sentences.en: What you're doing is telling a story.
sentences.zh: 你在做的是讲故事。

sentences.en: And that is sort of what I think about therapy in a simplistic way.
sentences.zh: 这也就是我以一种简单化的方式看待心理治疗的方式。

sentences.en: There's a lot of ways to take that to mean things that I don't mean.
sentences.zh: 有很多方法会把这句话曲解成我没有表达的意思。

sentences.en: But I do think that the narratives of our lives are sort of, like,
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为我们生活的叙事某种程度上，

sentences.en: encoded in these implicit assumptions and the way that we see the world and feel the world and react to the world and what we expect it to do for us and what we want from it.
sentences.zh: 被编码在这些隐性假设中，编码在我们看待世界、感受世界、对世界做出反应的方式中，编码在我们期望它为我们做什么以及我们对它的诉求中。

sentences.en: And the inability to see that and accept that is immaturity.
sentences.zh: 而无法看到这一点并接受这一点，就是一种不成熟。

sentences.en: And the inability to, you know, accept that you're not going to be enabled in this way or that the world fundamentally isn't fair or that, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 而且无法，你知道的，接受你不会以这种方式被纵容，或者世界根本是不公平的，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: you can't actually have the thing that you want on your terMs.
sentences.zh: 你其实无法按自己的条件得到你想要的东西。

sentences.en: You have to let go of your terms if you're going to get it.
sentences.zh: 如果你想得到它，你就必须放弃你的条件。

sentences.en: That's what interests me about therapy.
sentences.zh: 这才是心理治疗吸引我的地方。

sentences.en: And that's sort of what I'm talking about in this series.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在这个系列中一直在谈论的内容。

sentences.en: And you can be one of those people that's like, well, that isn't fair.
sentences.zh: 你可以当那种人，觉得“这不公平，

sentences.en: Like, you should, everyone should be logical.
sentences.zh: 每个人都应该是理性的”。

sentences.en: And if everyone just did a budget, then, like, there would be no need for government regulation because people could hold giant multilevel, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都做预算，那么，政府监管就完全没有必要了，因为人们仅凭购买决策就能牵制住那些庞大的多层级、

sentences.en: monopolies accountable just with their purchasing decisions.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，垄断企业。

sentences.en: Guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: People don't work that way.
sentences.zh: 人们根本不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: Like, you saying that you want everything to be debate club, that you want therapy to be that or politics to be that or philosophy to be that or whatever.
sentences.zh: 就像，你说你希望一切都变成辩论社，你希望心理治疗是那样的，或者政治是那样的，或者哲学是那样的，随便什么都行。

sentences.en: Like, that is your inability to accept that people are not that.
sentences.zh: 这其实暴露出你无法接受人类根本不是那样的现实。

sentences.en: They don't think that way and they never will.
sentences.zh: 他们不那样思考，而且永远不会。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's your thing to get over that we're not actually going to solve problems like by sitting there being like, and no true Scotsman, ad absurdum, ad hominem.
sentences.zh: 好了，所以这是你需要克服的心魔——我们实际上并不能通过坐在那里说“诉诸无苏格兰人、归谬法、人身攻击”来解决问题。

sentences.en: Like, there's a political party that has tried, you know, every other election to run a candidate who says, well,
sentences.zh: 就像，有个政党每隔一次选举就尝试推出这样一个候选人，他说，嗯，

sentences.en: I'm just going to go out and make like an incredibly empirically valid argument and tell people to go to page 500 of my website.
sentences.zh: 我就是要发表一个在经验上极其有效的论点，并告诉人们去看我网站的第500页。

sentences.en: And they always lose because whether or not you think people should behave the way that people are programmed, they are programmed the way they're programmed.
sentences.zh: 而他们总是失败，因为不管你认为人们是否应该按照某种方式行事，人类的底层编程就是这样的。

sentences.en: Whether or not you want to accept the way the brain works, it still works the way that it works.
sentences.zh: 不管你是否愿意接受大脑的运作方式，它依然是按它自己的方式在运作。

sentences.en: And, you know, part of the irony and the tension and the funniness of this is people who are studying essentially like the mind,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这其中充满讽刺、张力和滑稽的地方在于，那些本质上在研究心灵、

sentences.en: the self in philosophy and psychology won't accept the terms of their own and other people's minds enough to do it well.
sentences.zh: 研究哲学和心理学中的自我的人，却不愿意充分接受自己和他人心灵的运作规则，从而无法把它做好。

sentences.en: And I see, you know, basically self being studied better, you know, yeah, every hundred years, maybe you get somebody in philosophy, but generally by academic,
sentences.zh: 我看到，你知道的，基本上自我的研究做得更好——你知道的，对，每隔一百年，你可能会在哲学领域遇到某个厉害人物，但总体上，由学术界——

sentences.en: never thought I'd say this, I see it being studied better by academic psychology than I see it studied by academic philosophy.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过我会这么说，我发现学术心理学对自我的研究，要比学术哲学研究得更好。

sentences.en: So it's just like not a thing that I really dig into a ton.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像不是一个我真的会大量深入钻研的领域。

sentences.en: The reason why I think it's relevant here is because we wanted to deal with some of those philosophers who come out every hundred years and I think do something that's pretty incredible because they see through the last 200,
sentences.zh: 我之所以觉得它在这里有相关性，是因为我们想要探讨那些每隔百年才涌现一次的哲学家，我认为他们做了一些非常不可思议的事，因为他们看透了过去200、

sentences.en: 100 years of the world to anticipate the next hundred in a way that no one understands.
sentences.zh: 100年的世界，并以一种无人能懂的方式去预判未来的一百年。

sentences.en: Nietzsche is like the big figure that always gets credit for this because he's writing about it in a pretty on the nose way.
sentences.zh: 尼采就像是那个总是因此而备受赞誉的伟大人物，因为他用一种相当直白的方式在写这些东西。

sentences.en: He's like having a madman come in and say, hey, you know, y'all don't understand the new world that you're in.
sentences.zh: 他就像是让一个疯子走进来，然后说：“嘿，你们这群人根本不理解你们身处的新世界。”

sentences.en: And people are like, ha ha ha, you don't understand it because have you thought about how we can't see it and won't accept it yet?
sentences.zh: 而人们却说：“哈哈哈哈，你不懂，因为你想过我们为什么还看不到、也无法接受它吗？”

sentences.en: And he's like, oh, OK.
sentences.zh: 而他则说：“哦，好吧。”

sentences.en: And he's not really the mad one, you know, and he's sort of like Nietzsche sort of like giving an underhanded compliment to all of society always or at least, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且他其实并不是那个疯子，你知道的，他某种程度上就像是在给整个社会——或者至少是，

sentences.en: the time that he's writing in.
sentences.zh: 在他写作的那个时代——送上一记带有讽刺意味的恭维。

sentences.en: So, yeah, like there are all these these big philosophers that are interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，有所有这些伟大的哲学家，他们都很有趣。

sentences.en: But the reason why I ended talking about Slaughter Duke, even though I don't know a ton about him,
sentences.zh: 但我最终谈到彼得· Sloterdijk（斯洛特戴克）的原因是，尽管我对他的了解并不算特别多，

sentences.en: I'm probably not terribly well equipped enough to understand everything by him that I've read or heard him say, which there's not a ton of it in English either.
sentences.zh: 我可能也没有足够的知识储备去完全理解我读过的或者听他说过的他的所有观点，而且英文资料里关于他的内容也不算多。

sentences.en: Which is that's one of the reasons why I think these large language models and stuff is so nice as you can actually get translations of things that you couldn't otherwise get.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我认为这些大语言模型之类的东西这么棒的原因，因为你确实可以获得以前无法获得的翻译资料。

sentences.en: But I'm not a huge fan of the Silicon Valley stuff, but yeah, use it for what it can do.
sentences.zh: 虽然我并不是硅谷那一套东西的超级粉丝，但没错，能用它做什么就用它做什么。

sentences.en: But one of the reasons why I think he's so different is that like everyone else who's kind of mucking around right now is like either being incredibly postmodern and calling themselves post-postmodern and pretending to be different.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为他如此与众不同的原因之一在于，就像现在周围其他所有瞎混的人一样，要么变得极其后现代，自称为后-后现代，并假装自己与众不同。

sentences.en: But they're really not.
sentences.zh: 但他们其实并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: You know, like Zitek is not terribly different from Lacan in any way that is important.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如齐泽克在任何重要的方面其实和拉康都没有太大区别。

sentences.en: Like, yes, I know what they believe in, that they don't agree in, that they're making different points, but they're still part of the same movement trying not to be.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道他们信仰什么、他们有分歧的地方、他们提出了不同的观点，但他们仍然属于同一个试图假装自己不属于它的运动。

sentences.en: Or there's people out there like fighting against postmodernism and saying, actually,
sentences.zh: 或者还有人反对后现代主义，并声称：事实上，

sentences.en: we should go back because I want to retroject all this stuff and see another narrative into the history of whatever.

sentences.en: You know, Jordan Peterson has now decided he's a philosopher, you know, probably because he lost his license.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，乔丹·彼得森现在决定自己是个哲学家了，你知道的，大概是因为他丢了行医执照。

sentences.en: And it's a popular thing that people do, you know, like when you lose your job, instead of saying like, oh, oops, you say, oh, I'm a philosopher now.
sentences.zh: 这是人们常做的一件事，你知道的，当你失业时，你不会说“哦，哎呀”，而是会说“哦，我现在是个哲学家了”。

sentences.en: You know, the I lost my job to philosopher pipeline is a well-worn pathway, so good luck.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，“我失业了去当哲学家”是一条老生常谈的通途，所以祝你好运。

sentences.en: But, you know, people like him will make this argument that we really need to just go back in time and that like if you look at the first principles of everything,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，像他这样的人会提出这样的论点：我们真的需要回到过去，如果你审视一切的第一原理，

sentences.en: then they all justify these things that he wants you to think in a way that I don't think they do.
sentences.zh: 那么它们就会以一种我并不认同的方式，去为他想让你相信的事情提供正当性。

sentences.en: You know, like he'll say that Descartes is united with Aristotle because Descartes is facing the giants in doubt of saying,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如他会说笛卡尔与亚里士多德是一致的，因为笛卡尔正面对着怀疑的巨人，并说道：

sentences.en: I don't know any of my assumptions are true and the only one I can trust is myself.
sentences.zh: “我不知道我的任何假设是否为真，我唯一能信任的就是我自己。”

sentences.en: And so that is dealing with the same connection to the divine that Aristotle sees when he conceptualizes knowledge coming from the form that I'm thinking about.
sentences.zh: 所以这与亚里士多德在将知识概念化为来自我正在思考的形式时所看到的与神圣的联系是同一回事。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，我不知道。

sentences.en: Psychology 101, man, like sometimes it's not terribly wrong or reduced.
sentences.zh: 心理学101，老兄，有时候它并没有错得离谱或者被过度简化。

sentences.en: Like Descartes believes a pretty fundamentally different thing about knowledge than Aristotle.
sentences.zh: 就像笛卡尔关于知识的信念与亚里士多德有着相当根本的区别。

sentences.en: They're not the same.
sentences.zh: 他们是不一样的。

sentences.en: You can't really square that circle.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法把这个圆强行方化。

sentences.en: You can talk for a long time until they come back together in a loop.
sentences.zh: 你可以说上半天，直到它们重新汇合成一个圈。

sentences.en: But that tends to be him trying to convince himself of something.
sentences.zh: 但这往往只是他在试图说服自己相信什么东西。

sentences.en: And I'm not meaning to pick on Peterson.
sentences.zh: 我并不是故意要挑剔彼得森。

sentences.en: Like I'm just saying that there's a lot of people doing that for Vecchi or something.
sentences.zh: 我只是说有很多像瓦基（Vervaeke）之类的人也在这样做。还有另一个家伙，是个油管博主。

sentences.en: There's another guy that's like a YouTube guy.
sentences.zh: 我其实并不混那个圈子。

sentences.en: I don't really like live in that world.
sentences.zh: 但我看到的基本上就是这两种运动：一种是后现代主义假装自己不是后现代主义，

sentences.en: But those are the kind of the two movements I see is like postmodernism pretending not to be postmodernism,
sentences.zh: 我想后现代主义在这方面会很擅长，或者解构工具对你很有用，能让你假装自己不属于那个实际上已分崩离析成百万个碎片运动的一部分。

sentences.en: which I guess postmodernism is going to be like good at doing or the tools of deconstruction are going to be useful for you to pretend that you're not a part of the movement that you're a part of that is indivisible into a million parts.
sentences.zh: 另一种则是人们说：我不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And then people saying, I don't like that.
sentences.zh: 别这么干。

sentences.en: Don't do that.
sentences.zh: 别这么干。

sentences.en: Somebody like Slaughtergeek is not he's like one of the only people.
sentences.zh: 像 Slaughtergeek 这样的人可以说是凤毛麟角。

sentences.en: And again, like I don't love the guy.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我也不是多喜欢这家伙。

sentences.en: I don't know anything about him.
sentences.zh: 我对他的了解并不多。

sentences.en: You can't even get anything that he's written largely other than like the Spheres trilogy and critique and a couple other things.
sentences.zh: 除了《沉思三部曲》、评论文章以及其他一些东西之外，你基本上很难读到他写的大多数作品。

sentences.en: But like and, you know, there's things that he says that are insane and fascist, too.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，他也说过一些极其荒谬且带有法西斯色彩的话。

sentences.en: Like I'm not defending the person.
sentences.zh: 这并不是在为他这个人辩护。

sentences.en: The thing the reason that I and Heidegger is a Nazi, too.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，海德格尔其实也是个纳粹。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Like half of this stuff is built on following up on Dasein and those connections with time and the nature of ontology.
sentences.zh: 这其中的大半部分内容，都是建立在对“此在”（Dasein）的追随，以及它与时间还有本体论本质的联系之上的。

sentences.en: But the thing that is different about Slaughtergeek, the reason that I ended with him is I don't think he's doing the same thing that everyone else is.
sentences.zh: 但 Slaughtergeek 不同的一点在于，我之所以最后会提到他，是因为我觉得他做的事情和别人完全不一样。

sentences.en: And that's not really apparent yet.
sentences.zh: 这一点目前还不是很明显。

sentences.en: Like if there is going to be this new phase, if there is going to be this new thing that is anticipatory, it probably is going to be somebody like him.
sentences.zh: 如果说未来会有这样一个新阶段，如果会有这种具有前瞻性的新事物出现，那大概就会是像他这样的人。

sentences.en: You know, he's the one that's starting to see past the things that everyone else is fighting about.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是那个开始看透大家争论不休的事物本质的人。

sentences.en: And just the nature of the, you know, so much of the series, like if you take anything,
sentences.zh: 而这系列的本质，你知道的，如果你拿任何东西来……

sentences.en: get that conversation and therapy is a conversation between the nature of the self there and their relationship to the world around them.
sentences.zh: 把那场对话拿来，治疗就是自我本质与周围世界之间关系的一场对话。

sentences.en: And when that world is changing as fast as our world is changing, then we have to we're going to see not the nature, maybe.
sentences.zh: 当这个世界的变化速度和我们世界的变化速度一样快时，我们所看到的，也许就不是那种本质了。

sentences.en: And again, I don't want to be a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 再次声明，我可不想当什么哲学家。

sentences.en: Maybe the nature of the human self doesn't change that much.
sentences.zh: 也许人类自我的本质并没有发生多大变化。

sentences.en: But the reality of the human self changes quite a bit because the world around it is so different.
sentences.zh: 但人类自我的现实却发生了相当大的变化，因为周围的世界已经完全不同了。

sentences.en: Like I just walked you from there from the 70s to the mid 2000s on that part four and explained like why those forces change psychotherapy so much because people are bringing things into therapy that just didn't exist in the 60s,
sentences.zh: 就像我在第四部分里带你从 70 年代一路走到 2000 年代中期那样，我解释了这些力量为什么会极大地改变心理治疗，因为人们把 60 年代根本不存在的东西带进了治疗中，

sentences.en: like conceptions of life that weren't there.
sentences.zh: 比如以前根本不存在的生活观念。

sentences.en: And you just couldn't be Freud anymore.
sentences.zh: 你再也无法墨守弗洛伊德的那套了。

sentences.en: Like you had to start making these other things.
sentences.zh: 你不得不开始搞出这些别的东西。

sentences.en: A lot of those guesses are wrong.
sentences.zh: 其中很多猜测都是错的。

sentences.en: A lot of those guesses are overreactions to other things.
sentences.zh: 很多猜测其实是对其他事物的过度反应。

sentences.en: I'm doing that with my therapy.
sentences.zh: 我做心理治疗时也是这样。

sentences.en: I'm doing that with my series.
sentences.zh: 我做这个系列节目也是这样。

sentences.en: Like no one's an exception from it.
sentences.zh: 谁都无法例外。

sentences.en: Like I'm not a prophet.
sentences.zh: 我又不是什么先知。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I tend to think that it's safer to give the patient more control over their reality and that it is also safer to be more integrative in your approach so that when you're trying to understand the self in the world that the patient inhabits,
sentences.zh: 我倾向于认为，让患者对自己的现实拥有更多掌控权会更安全，而且在方法上采取更多元整合的方式也会更安全，这样当你在试图理解患者所处的自我与世界时，

sentences.en: you're being more flexible.
sentences.zh: 你会变得更有灵活性。

sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，我在治疗中受过伤害。

sentences.en: You know, the guy that was like wild and incompetent, I'm kind of laughing about it because it's so crazy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那个狂野又不称职的家伙，我现在说起来还有点想笑，因为实在太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But like I had PTSD from that, you know.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，因此我得了创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。

sentences.en: I had to go see another therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 我不得不去看另一个心理治疗师。

sentences.en: It's not.
sentences.zh: 并非如此。

sentences.en: If something like that has happened to you, I don't take it lightly.
sentences.zh: 如果这种事发生在你身上，我绝不会轻描淡写地对待。

sentences.en: And it was very painful when it happened to me.
sentences.zh: 这事发生在我身上时，真的非常痛苦。

sentences.en: I'm not, you know, here to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我今天来这里，你知道的，不是为了聊这个。

sentences.en: But, you know, this stuff is important.
sentences.zh: 但是，这些东西真的很重要。

sentences.en: And I see psychotherapy being more therapeutic than a lot of these other like disciplines that are basically talking about self and life.
sentences.zh: 我发现心理治疗比许多其他基本在探讨自我与人生的学科要更有治疗效果。

sentences.en: I love anthropology.
sentences.zh: 我热爱人类学。

sentences.en: I love sociology.
sentences.zh: 我热爱社会学。

sentences.en: I like philosophy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢哲学。

sentences.en: But I just don't swim in those waters.
sentences.zh: 但我只是不在那些领域里涉足太深。

sentences.en: You know, maybe the Jungian thing puts me in conversation with anthropology and self and philosophy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，荣格的理论或许让我能够与人类学、自我以及哲学展开对话。

sentences.en: But one of the things that I think that Peterson's doing that's not helpful and that a lot of these newer guys are doing just because like it works to sell a brand.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得彼得森（Peterson）所做的一件没有帮助的事，也是许多这些新潮人物正在做的事，仅仅是因为这招对兜售个人品牌很有效。

sentences.en: And to get people on YouTube to like leave a comment that's like, wow, I'm not smart enough to understand any of these words,
sentences.zh: 而且能吸引人们在 YouTube 上留言说：“哇，我智商太低了，根本听不懂这些词，

sentences.en: but I am smart enough to know that it's the smartest thing ever and that this guy's right.
sentences.zh: 但我足够聪明，能看出这是史上最牛的东西，这家伙绝对是对的。”

sentences.en: And it's like, okay, well, yeah, that isn't how that works.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，好吧，事情根本不是这样的。

sentences.en: But the thing that Peterson's doing is like a very surface level reading of Carl Jung and a very surface level reading of Mircea Eliade,
sentences.zh: 但彼得森在做的事情，是对卡尔·荣格（Carl Jung）非常表层化的解读，也是对米尔恰·伊利亚德（Mircea Eliade）非常表层化的解读，

sentences.en: where he's saying that like all religions are saying the same thing.
sentences.zh: 他声称所有的宗教讲的都是同一回事。

sentences.en: And then if you go in and you just shave off like every single bit of detail in the myth and everything from the Hebrew Bible or, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后如果你去深入挖掘，把神话中的每一个细节都剥离掉，把希伯来圣经里的所有内容都抹去，或者你知道的，

sentences.en: the Talmud or whatever that is actually making fun of like Babylonia or making fun of the Roman Empire and saying that those things are bad and that they'll get destroyed by kind of tweaking their myths.
sentences.zh: 比如塔木德或是其他什么东西，其实它们是在嘲讽巴比伦或者嘲讽罗马帝国，并指出那些东西是邪恶的，最终会被它们篡改后的神话所摧毁。

sentences.en: Like if you just take that all away, but underneath it really like all religion are the same and they just have the same myths and they just have the same archetypes.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这些统统抛开，只留下潜藏底层的核心，那就是所有宗教其实都一样，它们都有着相同的神话和原型。

sentences.en: I mean, I like the Jungian stuff, archetypes exist, but to separate like everything from culture in a way that that is that reductive and just be like,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我挺喜欢荣格的那套，原型确实存在，但如果以那种具有高度还原论倾向的方式把文化中的一切全部剥离开来，然后说，

sentences.en: we can use Jung to show us basically like the Cartesian principles.
sentences.zh: 我们能用荣格来向我们展示笛卡尔式的原则。

sentences.en: We can use this Jung in this way that is Cartesian to show us like all these things that are present inside of every myth.
sentences.zh: 我们可以用这种笛卡尔式的方式来运用荣格，向我们展示所有这些存在于每一个神话之中的事物。

sentences.en: So they're like first principles that we have to live by.
sentences.zh: 所以它们就像是我们必须遵循的第一原则。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just very apparent that he's doing that, not because that's like an interesting way to like help anybody or find knowledge or find anything new,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然他这么做，不是因为这是一种帮助任何人、寻找知识或发现新事物的有趣方式，

sentences.en: but because he believes a bunch of things that he wants you to believe.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他坚信了一堆他希望你也去相信的东西。

sentences.en: And he's spinning his tires in the mud intellectually to try and come up with a way, you know, the same thing Nietzsche's critiquing to say my belief that I want you to have,
sentences.zh: 他在思想上作茧自缚，试图想出一种方法——正如尼采所批判的那样——好让我所拥有、让你去信仰的信念，

sentences.en: that I like am so emotional about and desperately need to be your reality also and need to be true.
sentences.zh: 一个让我如此充满激情、迫切需要它也成为你的现实、并且必须成为真理的信念，

sentences.en: I've proved this true with reason, which is kind of a dangerous thing to do, I think, because like reason and logic and all of that debate clubby philosophy stuff,
sentences.zh: 我用理性证明了它是真的。我觉得这其实是一件很危险的事，因为理性、逻辑以及所有那些辩论社风格的哲学把戏，

sentences.en: I just think is silly.
sentences.zh: 我只觉得它们很蠢。

sentences.zh: 当你从常春藤盟校找来顶尖经济学家时，这项研究已经有10多年历史了，嗯，当你问他们：什么是货币？

sentences.en: They couldn't tell you that's happening to psychology, but with people, but with self.
sentences.zh: 他们答不上来，这正发生在心理学上，只不过是针对人，针对自我。

sentences.en: And that's scary.
sentences.zh: 这太吓人了。

sentences.en: That's, that's weird.
sentences.zh: 这太诡异了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, and I think, but academic psychology, they at least know the context of these arguments and like the history of it and the way that these YouTube influencers,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我认为，不过学院派心理学至少了解这些论点的语境、历史，以及YouTube网红们

sentences.en: like don't even begin to try and understand it's irrelevant to them.
sentences.zh: 甚至不愿去尝试理解的方式，这对他们来说无关紧要。

sentences.en: Um, and it's no like mistake that it's no like coincidence that they're all going to end up with this, like, um, spiritualism basically in, um, philosophy,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们最终都会走向某种基本上属于哲学中的精神主义，这绝非巧合，

sentences.en: because people think the philosophy is smart yet.
sentences.zh: 因为人们觉得哲学现在听起来还很聪明。

sentences.en: It was people wrestling with questions that aren't the one we're wrestling with now, but you need to make history, this like projection.
sentences.zh: 那是人们在与我们现在不再纠结的问题作斗争，但你需要把历史变成一种投射。

sentences.en: You need to project into history that it's this, um, you know, huge, uh, journey to get to where you are, to make your point uniquely relevant.
sentences.zh: 你需要把历史投射为，你知道的，通往你现在所在位置的一段宏大旅程，以此让你的观点显得独特而相关。

sentences.en: And when you do that, um, what you, what you're, you're always going to end up with something like Aristotle,
sentences.zh: 当你这样做时，嗯，你最终得到的总是类似于亚里士多德的东西，

sentences.en: because Aristotle is saying that the reason that you have the thought is that the form of the thing, like the idea, the knowledge itself is out there in the universe.
sentences.zh: 因为亚里士多德认为，你之所以会有这个想法，是因为事物的形式，也就是理念、知识本身，就存在于宇宙之中。

sentences.en: And it is, you are resonating with it when you were having that thought.
sentences.zh: 当你产生这个想法时，你是在与之产生共鸣。

sentences.en: It's not that you were taking an information and then creating something in your brain.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你在获取信息，然后在大脑中创造了什么。

sentences.en: It's that you have a divine connection to knowledge, a divine connection to the proof, to the truth.
sentences.zh: 而是你与知识、与证明、与真理有着神圣的连接。

sentences.en: And like Aristotle didn't think that you had ideas and the way that Descartes did.
sentences.zh: 亚里士多德不认为你拥有想法，不像笛卡尔那样。

sentences.en: He thought that ideas had you.
sentences.zh: 他认为想法拥有你。

sentences.en: So when you're an archetypal psychologist who is essentially possessed by the ideas that you're talking about,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你是一个本质上被你所谈论的想法所附体的原型心理学家时，

sentences.en: and of course you're going to be coming back to how something like that is right.
sentences.zh: 你当然会回过头来赞同这种观点是正确的。

sentences.en: But when you can't admit that, you're going to get just flailing around trying to solve an emotional problem intellectually
sentences.zh: 但当你无法承认这一点时，你就会手足无措，试图用智力去解决一个情感问题，

sentences.en: by using all of this like logical rubrics and like crazy Rube Goldberg machines of thought to try and build some way to prove that the thing that you need to believe is empirical.
sentences.zh: 使用所有这些逻辑准则和疯狂的思想鲁布·戈德堡机械，试图建立某种方式来证明你需要相信的东西是经验性的。

sentences.en: It's not just that you need to believe it because it justifies who you are and what you want to do.
sentences.zh: 不仅是因为你需要相信它，因为它证明了你是谁以及你想做什么。

sentences.en: It's that it is handed down by God and that is something that is a release valve for self
sentences.zh: 而是它是上帝传下来的，这是对自我的一种泄压阀，

sentences.en: and this decaying relationship between self and world that psychotherapy isn't really holding
sentences.zh: 以及心理治疗无法真正维系的自我与世界之间日渐衰落的关系，

sentences.en: that society has as an inevitability if you don't build a better therapy.
sentences.zh: 如果构建不出更好的疗法，社会就必然会承受这一切。

sentences.en: Like if you continue to say CBT and ABA and ultra medical and ultra whatever, maybe they still come to you.
sentences.zh: 就像如果你继续说CBT、ABA和超医疗以及超别的什么，也许人们仍然会来找你。

sentences.en: Maybe they still think that what you're doing is helpful.
sentences.zh: 也许他们仍然认为你做的事是有帮助的。

sentences.en: Maybe they still, maybe you still make a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 也许他们仍然，也许你依然能赚很多钱。

sentences.en: You know, I think even those things are going to start to be in danger, but maybe that still happens.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为即使是这些事情也将开始面临危险，但也许那仍然会发生。

sentences.en: But where the soul goes, you know, where the trauma and the intuition and the nightmares of our culture goes is onto YouTube.
sentences.zh: 然而，灵魂的去向，你知道的，我们文化的创伤、直觉和噩梦的去向，都涌向了YouTube。

sentences.en: So do better like psychotherapy, please do better.
sentences.zh: 所以心理治疗请做好一点，求求你们做好一点。
